title: Efficacy and modes of action of an age-sensitive telehealth group therapy to reduce clinical depression (with and without anxiety) in older adults (VISION-AGE)
summary:
As we grow older, many things change – in our daily lives, in our bodies, and in the way we view life. Depression is one of the most common mental health conditions in later life and is often accompanied by anxiety. Despite the high need for treatment, older adults rarely receive appropriate therapeutic support.
Vision-Age is a scientific study that examines the effectiveness of an age-sensitive online group therapy program for people aged 68 and older to treat depression and co-occurring anxiety. We compare our psychotherapeutic program with a non-clinical discussion group that is offered in the same digital group format and with the same duration. Both programs aim to reduce depressive and anxious symptoms and to enhance psychological well-being. Our goal is to determine whether the psychotherapeutic intervention is clinically superior.
Participants in the study will be supported over a period of 20 weeks by experienced professionals – either from the field of psychotherapy (intervention group / Arm 1) or from senior assistance (discussion group / Arm 2). The digital group sessions take place once a week and last 100 minutes. In addition, participants will have four individual online meetings with their group facilitator.
Digital scientific assessments will be conducted both before and during the group program. This allows us to comprehensively evaluate the effectiveness of the project.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• the person has the capacity to give informed consent, voluntarily agree to participate in the study
• they are diagnosed with mild or moderate unipolar depressive symptoms associated with one of the following ICD-10 diagnoses: F32.0/1, F33.0/1, F38.1/8, F41.2 or F43.2 based on a clinical interview 
• they have clinically relevant depressive symptoms based on self-report
• they are not taking psychoactive medications or are taking a stable dosage for at least six weeks prior to study entry
• they have an indication for participation in group psychotherapy
• sufficient language and communication skills in German 
• functioning, stable internet connection and basic IT skills
Exclusion criteria:
• very severe depressive symptoms associated with one of the following ICD-10 diagnoses F32.2 or F33.2 based on the clinical interview  
• very severe depressive symptoms based on the self-report 
• very severe anxiety symptoms or symptoms of panic disorder or specific phobia that mandate in vivo exposure
• acute suicidal tendencies
• signs of or they have been diagnosed with dementia or mild cognitive impairment 
• signs of or they have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder or schizophrenia
• physical illness in the terminal phase
• plan to change their intake of psychoactive medications before enrolment or during the study
• receiving psychotherapy while participating in the study
• communication difficulties and visual or hearing impairments that would severely affect an individual’s ability to participate in the study
